paragraphs: Graph neural networks need to move information across a graph to connect distant nodes. Repeated propagation can also make node representations too similar, a problem called oversmoothing. This paper studies that tension and extends the mathematical treatment of oversmoothing from undirected graphs to directed graphs, where connections have an orientation.

The authors extend Dirichlet energy, a measure used to study variation across a graph, through a directed symmetrically normalized Laplacian. They then propose fractional graph Laplacian neural ordinary differential equations. These describe nonlocal dynamics, providing a way to model information movement beyond immediate neighbors within a continuous evolution framework.

The theoretical results show that the approach can transmit information between distant nodes while keeping long-distance jumps unlikely. It also permits more flexible behavior in how Dirichlet energy converges, which mitigates oversmoothing. Experiments on synthetic and real graphs cover directed and undirected connections and different levels of homophily, meaning how often similar nodes connect. These results support the method’s applicability across varied graph structures.
neurips-2023-a-fractional-graph-laplacia.tldr: Fractional graph dynamics help information reach distant nodes while mitigating oversmoothing across directed and undirected graphs.

paragraphs: Deep reinforcement learning can struggle when its learning signals fluctuate strongly. High variance can interfere with convergence and make continuous control tasks difficult to learn reliably. This paper introduces the long N-step surrogate stage reward, or LNSS, as a way to estimate the reward signal using information from a longer sequence of future rewards.

The central change concerns the reward supplied to learning. Instead of relying on a single step’s reward alone, LNSS draws on a longer reward trajectory. The authors incorporate this estimator into existing deep reinforcement learning algorithms, including DDPG, D4PG, and TD3, and evaluate them in DeepMind Control Suite and OpenAI Gym environments.

Across those evaluations, the authors report improvements in average reward, convergence speed, and learning success, alongside reduced variance in rewards and Q-values. Their analysis also establishes an exponential reduction in an upper bound on Q-value variance relative to the corresponding single-step methods. That theoretical result concerns the variance bound; the reported improvements in actual learning performance come from the experiments.
neurips-2023-a-long-n-step-surrogate-sta.tldr: LNSS uses longer reward trajectories to reduce variance and improve learning in evaluated continuous control tasks.

paragraphs: Meta learning aims to transfer experience across tasks so that a model can adapt quickly to a new one. Optimizing average training performance, however, can leave a subset of tasks with very poor adaptation outcomes. This paper focuses on those difficult cases, which matter especially when a bad outcome carries substantial risk.

The authors formulate meta learning from a distributionally robust perspective and train using tail task risk. This shifts attention toward the high-risk portion of the task distribution. They use a two-stage strategy as a heuristic for solving the robust learning problem, with the aim of controlling the worst adaptation cases at a specified probabilistic level.

Experiments show that the method can improve robustness to task distributions and lower the conditional average risk among the worst adaptation outcomes. The contribution is therefore about improving the unfavorable end of the performance distribution, rather than reporting only its overall average. The probabilistic framing matters: the stated objective concerns a selected level of tail risk, not a guarantee that every possible task will adapt successfully.
neurips-2023-a-simple-yet-effective-stra.tldr: Training meta learners on tail task risk can reduce poor adaptation outcomes and improve robustness across task distributions.

paragraphs: A model deployed in a new environment may encounter both unfamiliar input conditions and categories absent from training. Many domain generalization methods address the first change while assuming that the category set stays fixed. This paper studies Open Test-Time Domain Generalization, where both changes can occur in unseen test data.

The proposed CODA framework has two stages. During training, it makes representations of known source classes more compact and introduces virtual unknown classes into the representation space. This gives the model a training objective that explicitly shapes the boundary between known categories and potential unknowns, rather than treating all future inputs as members of familiar classes.

At test time, CODA further trains to clarify the separation between known and unknown samples. This stage addresses the difficulty of adapting to target data while limiting catastrophic forgetting. Experiments on standard domain generalization datasets show that CODA can substantially outperform the previous best method and improve the balance of classification accuracy for known and unknown classes. The findings support handling category novelty and domain shift together.
neurips-2023-coda-generalizing-to-open-a.tldr: CODA combines compact class representations with test-time adaptation to handle unfamiliar domains and previously unseen categories.

paragraphs: Generative models are expensive to train, making reuse attractive when a new task calls for a different output distribution. Combining existing models could help, but iterative generators introduce a particular difficulty: their intermediate steps must work together to produce the intended final distribution. A composition must therefore coordinate the generation process and respect its balance conditions.

This paper introduces Compositional Sculpting, a general approach for specifying combinations of iterative generative processes. It also develops a sampling method based on classifier guidance. The authors demonstrate how the approach applies to both GFlowNets and diffusion models, connecting the composition idea to two different families of iterative generators.

Two highlighted operations are the harmonic mean and contrast between component distributions, with extensions to more than two components. These operations provide concrete ways to specify a desired composition that the sampling procedure can pursue. Empirical results cover image and molecule generation. The contribution is a framework for defining and sampling such compositions, with demonstrations in both domains rather than a stated universal performance advantage.
neurips-2023-compositional-sculpting-of-.tldr: Compositional Sculpting defines combinations of iterative generators and uses classifier guidance to sample from them.

paragraphs: EEG signals contain both activity associated with a task and differences associated with the person being measured. Noise and variation across people make these components difficult to separate. This paper asks whether explicitly representing task content and subject style can support signal conversion and representations that generalize across subjects.

The authors propose CSLP-AE, an autoencoder framework that directly trains for EEG conversion. Its latent representation is split into components, and contrastive learning guides those components to represent subject identity and task information separately. The design draws inspiration from voice conversion, where separating what is expressed from who expresses it is also useful.

Compared with conventional supervised, autoencoder, and contrastive training approaches, CSLP-AE produces favorable generalizable characterizations of subjects and tasks. It also enables zero-shot conversion between previously unseen subjects. The reported experiments concern EEG specifically. The authors present the architecture as a broader framework for separating content and style in biological signals, but its demonstrated conversion results remain within the EEG setting studied.
neurips-2023-cslp-ae-a-contrastive-split.tldr: CSLP-AE separates task and subject information in EEG representations, enabling signal conversion between unseen subjects.

paragraphs: Outsourcing a classification task creates an incentive problem when the party doing the learning has interests that differ from the party requesting it. Predictive performance can suffer even when both parties act rationally. This paper develops a theoretical framework for designing payments that encourage accurate learning under such delegation.

The framework models the relationship as a principal-agent game and uses performance-based contracts. The authors define contracts that are optimal in budget terms and prove that, under their assumptions, these contracts have a simple threshold structure. In the case with two possible agent actions, the optimality result is equivalent to the Neyman-Pearson lemma, connecting incentive design with statistical hypothesis testing.

The empirical work examines whether such contracts can be constructed from small-scale data using learning curves and scaling laws. Results demonstrate that this construction is possible in the studied settings, with both predictive and economic outcomes evaluated on synthetic and real classification tasks. The work thus combines a conditional mathematical characterization of contract structure with evidence about how those contracts can be estimated.
neurips-2023-delegated-classification-e9.tldr: A principal-agent framework identifies simple performance-based contracts that can incentivize accurate outsourced classification.

paragraphs: Evaluating a reinforcement learning policy depends partly on how the environment’s states are represented. A detailed representation preserves distinctions, but its complexity can make estimation harder with limited data. This paper introduces Distributional Maximum Entropy Policy Evaluation, a framework that makes representation complexity an explicit part of policy evaluation.

The authors derive a generalization-error bound that depends on the complexity of the state representation. They then use this relationship to guide representation learning through structural risk minimization. Their concrete algorithm, D-Max-Ent Progressive Factorization, represents states through aggregation functions and gradually refines the resulting groups.

The refinement balances two competing effects. Keeping more distinctions preserves information and reduces bias, while combining states reduces the effective number of states and can reduce variance. This gives the algorithm a principled reason to choose a particular level of detail. Illustrative numerical simulations follow the expected theoretical behavior and show how useful aggregation depends on the available sample regime. The stated evidence supports this relationship between representation granularity and data availability.
neurips-2023-distributional-policy-evalu.tldr: A maximum entropy framework guides policy evaluation toward state representations that balance information preservation and estimation complexity.

paragraphs: Face recognition systems represent faces using facial templates. This paper studies template inversion: reconstructing a face image from that representation and using it to impersonate the represented person. The research examines whether a template can expose enough identity information to create an image accepted by a recognition system.

The method learns a mapping from facial templates into the intermediate latent space of a pretrained face generator within a GAN-based framework. The generator then produces realistic, high-resolution face reconstructions. The authors define five attack settings based on the adversary’s knowledge and the target recognition system, covering both whitebox and blackbox scenarios.

Experiments report high attack success rates in the studied whitebox and blackbox settings. Reconstructed images also transfer to recognition systems using a different feature extractor, showing that their usefulness for impersonation can extend beyond the original system. The authors additionally investigate which regions of reconstructed images influence successful attacks. Together, the findings demonstrate the evaluated systems’ vulnerability to identity information recovered from facial templates.
neurips-2023-face-reconstruction-from-fa.tldr: Mapping facial templates into a pretrained generator reconstructs faces that successfully impersonate subjects in evaluated recognition systems.

paragraphs: Contextual bandit algorithms choose an action using available information and then learn from its reward. Standard formulations place all relevant context before the choice. This paper considers settings where useful information arrives afterward, such as viewing duration or playback speed after a user selects recommended content.

The authors formulate a contextual bandit problem with these post-serving contexts and introduce poLinUCB to use them for more efficient online learning. Under standard assumptions, the algorithm achieves a tight regret guarantee. Regret measures the accumulated cost of learning to make good choices, so this result characterizes the algorithm’s decision quality over time.

The proof relies on a generalized, noise-robust version of the Elliptical Potential Lemma, a mathematical tool used in bandit analysis. This extension accommodates noisy data and is needed for the new setting. Tests on synthetic and real-world datasets show substantial benefits from using information observed after selection, along with superior performance over the compared approaches. The results support treating follow-up context as a learning resource.
neurips-2023-follow-ups-also-matter-impr.tldr: poLinUCB uses context observed after an action to improve contextual bandit learning, with conditional regret guarantees and empirical benefits.

paragraphs: Learning a concept from a few examples requires considering possible explanations without making inference unmanageably difficult. Rich hypothesis spaces offer many explanations, but searching them can be expensive. This paper develops a model intended to capture humans’ ability to learn across a broad range of concepts while keeping the reasoning process tractable.

A language model first proposes candidate hypotheses written in natural language. A Bayesian reasoning stage then adjusts their weights using a prior and a likelihood. These components separate hypothesis generation from evaluation: proposals supply possible explanations, while the weighting process considers their initial plausibility and how well they account for the observed examples.

The authors estimate the prior from human data and use the resulting model to predict human judgments on learning problems involving numbers and sets. The covered concepts include generative, discriminative, propositional, and higher-order forms. The finding is that this combination can model judgments across those varied concept types. Its human-like behavior is tied to the studied learning problems and the use of human data to estimate prior preferences.
neurips-2023-human-like-few-shot-learnin.tldr: Language-generated hypotheses, reweighted through Bayesian reasoning with a human-derived prior, predict human judgments across varied concept-learning tasks.

paragraphs: Repeated image compression can progressively change an image. An idempotent codec is designed to remain stable when its output is compressed again. Earlier approaches achieved this using invertible transforms, but this paper shows that full invertibility is a sufficient condition rather than a necessary requirement for that stability.

The authors identify right-invertibility as a weaker condition that can support idempotence. Relaxing the requirement makes a wider family of transforms available for codec design. They build a learned codec around this observation using blocked convolution and null-space enhancement, turning the mathematical distinction into a concrete compression method.

Experiments report state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance among idempotent codecs, meaning a favorable balance between compressed size and reconstruction quality. The authors also relax right-invertibility to create a near-idempotent version. After 50 recompression rounds, that version shows substantially less quality decay than the other near-idempotent codecs compared. These results distinguish exact recompression stability from an approximate variant that empirically limits accumulated degradation.
neurips-2023-idempotent-learned-image-co.tldr: Right-invertible transforms enable a broader class of recompression-stable learned codecs with strong reported rate-distortion performance.

paragraphs: Auxiliary learning uses additional tasks and data to help a primary task. Choosing useful auxiliary material often requires domain knowledge, and poorly chosen material can hurt the main objective. This paper proposes DTG-AuxL, which jointly generates auxiliary data and tasks rather than relying solely on reweighting manually collected ones.

The framework contains a feature generator and a label generator, allowing it to construct both inputs and their associated learning targets. A bi-level optimization procedure connects this generation process to the primary task. At the lower level, the task model learns from generated data and tasks. At the upper level, the generator receives an implicit gradient from the primary loss and an explicit gradient from an instance regularization term.

This arrangement makes the primary learning objective a source of guidance for auxiliary generation. Experiments across multiple auxiliary learning scenarios show consistent improvements over the compared methods, with particularly strong benefits when manually supplied auxiliary data and tasks are unhelpful. The findings support jointly designing what auxiliary examples contain and what the model is asked to learn from them.
neurips-2023-joint-data-task-generation-.tldr: DTG-AuxL jointly generates auxiliary features and labels, using the primary task’s loss to guide their usefulness.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning must learn from an existing dataset without collecting new interactions. Many algorithms require that this dataset cover the state-action space uniformly. This paper develops value-based methods with learning guarantees under a narrower coverage requirement: the offline data need only provide coverage relative to a single policy.

The guarantees also require realizability of an entropy-regularized Q-function and an additional function defined through a minimax saddle-point problem. Realizability means that the selected function classes can represent the functions required by the analysis. The authors establish an analogous result for ordinary Q-functions, extending the treatment beyond the entropy-regularized setting.

To build the algorithms, the authors express value estimation as nonlinear convex optimization and derive minimax losses through Lagrange functions. These losses support convergence guarantees measured on the offline data and probabilistic approximate-correctness guarantees for learning. The contribution is a conditional theoretical route to offline learning with partial coverage. Its weaker coverage requirement remains paired with the stated representation assumptions, rather than eliminating assumptions about the data and function classes altogether.
neurips-2023-offline-minimax-soft-q-lear.tldr: Minimax value-learning methods obtain offline reinforcement learning guarantees under single-policy coverage and stated realizability assumptions.

paragraphs: A proper learning algorithm must return a predictor from the hypothesis class it is learning. For adversarial robustness, finite VC dimension alone does not ensure that such learning is possible under the usual probabilistic guarantees. This paper investigates whether relaxing the worst-case robust loss can restore proper learnability.

The authors identify a family of relaxed robust losses for which VC classes are properly PAC learnable. The required sample complexity is close to that of standard PAC learning. This establishes that some changes to the robustness objective can make proper learning feasible without a large increase in the amount of training data required.

The paper also proves a negative result: an existing, natural relaxation still cannot guarantee proper learning from finite VC dimension alone. The choice of relaxation therefore matters; weakening worst-case robustness does not automatically remove the difficulty. Finally, the authors provide new generalization guarantees for adversarially robust empirical risk minimization. Together, these results clarify which forms of relaxed robustness support learning and which retain a fundamental obstacle.
neurips-2023-on-proper-learnability-betw.tldr: Some relaxations of worst-case robust loss restore proper PAC learnability for VC classes, while another natural relaxation does not.

paragraphs: Deep Q-networks combine value learning with practical mechanisms such as target networks, experience replay, and exploration. These ingredients complicate theoretical analysis. This paper studies convergence and sample complexity for DQN with epsilon-greedy exploration, a policy that balances choosing the currently preferred action with exploring other actions.

The authors analyze an iterative procedure in which epsilon decreases over time and prove geometric convergence to the optimal Q-value function. Geometric convergence describes error shrinking at a multiplicative rate across iterations. The analysis addresses a practical exploration strategy and the training structure that earlier theoretical treatments had left underexplored or simplified through substantial overparameterization.

A central result identifies a trade-off in exploration strength. Higher epsilon values enlarge the convergence region but slow convergence, while lower values have the opposite effect. This means the analysis connects exploration to both the range of starting conditions that permit convergence and the speed of learning within that range. Experiments support these theoretical insights. The convergence statement applies to the analyzed procedure, rather than establishing unconditional convergence for every DQN implementation.
neurips-2023-on-the-convergence-and-samp.tldr: An analysis of epsilon-greedy DQN links stronger exploration to a larger convergence region but slower convergence.

paragraphs: Generalization in reinforcement learning means using experience to make good decisions in environments beyond those used for training. Much prior work emphasizes representation learning. This paper investigates another factor: whether the agent’s exploration strategy changes the usefulness of what it learns for unfamiliar environments.

Experiments in a tabular contextual decision process show that exploration can do more than help find a good training policy. It can also acquire knowledge that supports decisions in unseen environments. Motivated by this observation, the authors introduce Exploration via Distributional Ensemble, or EDE, which uses an ensemble of Q-value distributions to encourage visits to states with high epistemic uncertainty.

Epistemic uncertainty concerns what the model does not yet know, making it a signal for directing further exploration. EDE achieves strong performance on both Procgen and Crafter, benchmarks involving high-dimensional observations and generalization. The authors identify it as the first value-based approach to do so on both. The results support treating exploration as part of generalization strategy, alongside the choice of learned representation.
neurips-2023-on-the-importance-of-explor.tldr: EDE explores states with high model uncertainty, supporting strong generalization performance on Procgen and Crafter.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate samples through repeated denoising, making inference computationally expensive. Quantization reduces numerical precision and can lower model size and computation without retraining, but it introduces errors that can disrupt the denoising process. This paper develops PTQD to account for those errors and preserve sample quality.

PTQD separates quantization error into a component correlated with the full-precision counterpart and an uncorrelated residual. It corrects the correlated component using an estimated correlation coefficient. For the residual, it removes mean bias and adjusts the denoising variance schedule to absorb additional variance. These corrections connect quantization noise to the noise already modeled by diffusion.

The method also varies precision across denoising steps, favoring lower bitwidths early and higher precision later to maintain signal quality. Experiments report better samples than previous post-training quantized diffusion methods. For LDM-4 on ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution, the reported FID increase over full precision is only 0.06 while bit operations fall by a factor of 19.9. This quantifies a computation-quality trade-off, rather than a direct wall-clock speed measurement.
neurips-2023-ptqd-accurate-post-training.tldr: PTQD corrects quantization noise and varies precision across denoising steps to reduce diffusion computation while preserving sample quality.

paragraphs: This paper studies restless bandits over an unlimited time horizon, with performance measured by average reward. The goal is to compute policies whose gap from optimal performance shrinks as the number of arms grows. Earlier asymptotic optimality results depended on the uniform global attractor property, an assumption that is difficult to verify.

The proposed Follow-the-Virtual-Advice framework converts a policy for one arm into a policy for the full collection. It simulates the single-arm policy separately for each arm and carefully steers each real state toward its simulated counterpart. An appropriate instantiation achieves an optimality gap of order one divided by the square root of the number of arms.

The assumptions differ between time settings. In discrete time, the result uses a simpler synchronization condition that includes some instances violating the earlier attractor assumption. In continuous time, only the standard unichain condition is required. The contribution is thus an asymptotic guarantee that avoids the difficult attractor requirement in both settings while retaining the specific conditions stated for each.
neurips-2023-restless-bandits-with-avera.tldr: Simulated single-arm advice yields asymptotically optimal restless-bandit policies without the uniform global attractor assumption.

paragraphs: Learning to detect objects in LiDAR point clouds without training labels requires a signal that distinguishes useful detections from poor ones. This paper adapts ideas from reinforcement learning with human feedback to unsupervised object discovery. It replaces direct human feedback with simple heuristics that score candidate bounding boxes.

The heuristics are combined into a reward function whose scores positively correlate with bounding-box accuracy. Boxes containing objects receive higher scores than boxes without objects. Starting from the detector’s own predictions, the method explores candidate boxes and uses gradient updates to reinforce those receiving higher rewards. This turns heuristic preferences into a training signal for improving the detector.

Experiments show higher accuracy and training that is orders of magnitude faster than the compared prior object-discovery methods. The findings indicate that a useful reward can support learning without labeled training boxes in the studied setting. The connection to human feedback is methodological: the approach imitates preferences through heuristics, and the reported improvements come from this reward-driven training process.
neurips-2023-reward-finetuning-for-faste.tldr: Heuristic rewards improve label-free LiDAR object discovery, with reported gains in accuracy and orders-of-magnitude faster training.

paragraphs: Medical image analysis networks can be expensive to run, especially on volumetric inputs. Changing their internal downsampling and upsampling factors offers a way to trade accuracy for computational cost. Exploring that trade-off by training a separate network for every setting, however, can itself require substantial computation.

Scale-Space HyperNetworks address this expense by learning a spectrum of convolutional networks with different internal rescaling factors. A single trained SSHN characterizes an accuracy-efficiency Pareto curve: a collection of choices offering different balances between prediction quality and computational demand. This lets a user select an appropriate rescaling factor at inference time.

Across several medical imaging applications, the resulting models match and sometimes exceed the performance obtained by training many separate fixed-scale networks. Comparisons with both fixed and dynamic rescaling strategies show consistently better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs at a fraction of the training cost. The practical contribution is therefore flexibility after training, together with a less expensive way to discover the available operating choices in the evaluated applications.
neurips-2023-scale-space-hypernetworks-f.tldr: A single Scale-Space HyperNetwork learns multiple accuracy-efficiency options for medical imaging at reduced training cost.

paragraphs: Learning a dynamical system from observations does not automatically ensure that its predictions respect known rules. Those rules may express conservation laws or restrict which states are allowed. This paper introduces stabilized neural differential equations, or SNDEs, to incorporate explicit constraints into learned continuous-time dynamics.

The approach adds a stabilization term to the original dynamics. Constraints are represented as a manifold, the set of states satisfying the specified relationships. The authors prove that the added term makes this manifold asymptotically stable, providing a mathematical account of attraction toward the constraint set. That stability property is the central mechanism for enforcing the known structure.

The method is designed to work with all common neural differential equation models, allowing constraints to be added across existing model families. Extensive empirical evaluations show improvements over existing methods while accommodating a broader range of constraints during training. The result combines a stability guarantee with experimental performance evidence: the theory characterizes the constrained dynamics, while the experiments demonstrate the method’s usefulness in the evaluated learning settings.
neurips-2023-stabilized-neural-different.tldr: SNDEs add a stabilization term that makes explicit constraint manifolds asymptotically stable within learned differential equations.

paragraphs: Gaussian processes offer uncertainty estimates and interpretable kernel parameters, such as a lengthscale describing how far correlations extend. Choosing the kernel can nevertheless be difficult. Deep Gaussian processes learn more flexible structures, but common constructions sacrifice either this interpretability or the ability to learn lower-dimensional embeddings, and can develop problematic behavior.

Thin and Deep Gaussian Processes combine these two approaches. Each layer defines locally linear transformations of the original inputs. This retains latent embeddings while preserving the interpretation of kernel lengthscales. The construction is designed to discover lower-dimensional structure without the manifold pathologies associated with the prior approaches discussed by the authors.

Theoretical and experimental results support three claims: the model is specifically suited to finding lower-dimensional manifolds, behaves well as layers are added, and performs well on standard benchmark datasets. The contribution is a particular architecture that joins representation learning with interpretable correlation structure. Its reported behavior with increasing depth also addresses a difficulty that can make deeper probabilistic models harder to fit and interpret.
neurips-2023-thin-and-deep-gaussian-proc.tldr: Thin and Deep Gaussian Processes learn lower-dimensional structure while retaining interpretable lengthscales and favorable behavior with depth.

paragraphs: Estimating 3D pose from multiple views often requires large amounts of annotated training data. This is particularly difficult for animals. The paper introduces Triangulation Residual loss, or TR loss, to use unlabeled multiview observations for training by checking whether predicted keypoints agree geometrically across the available views.

Earlier epipolar consistency objectives compare pairs of views locally. TR loss instead enforces global multiview consistency. Starting with initial 2D keypoint estimates, it minimizes the smallest singular value of the triangulation matrix. This scalar training signal allows end-to-end fine-tuning of the 2D detector without requiring 3D supervision.

On Human3.6M, the method reports a state-of-the-art mean per-joint position error of 25.8 millimeters and a competitive 28.7 millimeters using only 5% of the 2D labeled training data. Experiments with animals, including mice, also demonstrate data-efficient training. The findings show how geometric agreement among views can supply useful supervision, reducing dependence on labeled poses while improving the detector that provides the initial 2D estimates.
neurips-2023-triangulation-residual-loss.tldr: TR loss uses global multiview geometry to fine-tune pose detectors without 3D labels and with limited 2D annotation.

paragraphs: Uniform convergence guarantees connect measured training performance with population performance across an entire hypothesis class. This paper establishes such guarantees for Gaussian data using the complexity of the hypothesis class and the regularity of the square root of the loss. Its focus is the mathematical condition needed to obtain these guarantees.

The bounds depend on Rademacher complexity and a Lipschitz constant for the square-root loss. The latter controls how quickly the square root of the loss can change. This differs from requiring a Lipschitz derivative, the smoothness condition used in earlier results, and allows the analysis to cover a broader family of losses.

That broader family includes nonsmooth losses relevant to phase retrieval and ReLU regression. The framework also recovers and helps explain optimistic-rate and interpolation learning guarantees. The contribution is therefore both an extension of applicable loss functions and a common perspective on existing learning results. Gaussian data remain an explicit condition of the stated guarantees; expanding the loss family does not remove that distributional setting.
neurips-2023-uniform-convergence-with-sq.tldr: Square-root Lipschitz conditions extend uniform convergence guarantees for Gaussian data to a broader class of losses, including nonsmooth ones.
